root.name: Center Game: Lanc-Arnold Gambit
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. d4 exd4 3. Nf3 Bc5 4. c3

overview: In 1.e4 e5 2.d4 exd4 3.Nf3 Bc5 White plays 4.c3, a gambit offering the c-pawn. After 4...dxc3 5.Bc4 (the Schippler Gambit) White has given two pawns for fast development and attacking chances against f7, while Black can take with 5...cxb2 6.Bxb2 and consolidate with ...d6 and ...Nf6. Black can also decline with ...d3 or ...d6. It is a rare, aggressive line.

white_ideas.idea: Offer two pawns for a lead in development with Bc4 and Qb3
Attack f7 with Bc4, Ng5 and Qb3
Recapture on b2 with the bishop and use open diagonals

black_ideas.idea: Take the pawns and consolidate with ...d6, ...Nf6 and ...Be6
Defend f7 and trade queens or the active bishop
Return material at a good moment

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with White two pawns down and Black pieces on active squares

character.notes: Pure gambit play with attacks on f7 and mutual tactics.

gambit.notes: Black can keep both pawns if he defends accurately.

soundness.notes: Considered unsound at a high level.

structure.notes: Open centre, open lines for the bishops.

level.notes: Dubious, so not a first repertoire choice.

sublines_that_differ.name: Schippler Gambit
sublines_that_differ.how: White gives two pawns for attack on f7.

character.reason: White sacrifices pawns for a quick attack; forcing and tactical.

gambit.reason: White gives up pawns for development and Black can keep them.

soundness.reason: Strong players consider it unsound and Black can consolidate.

structure.reason: Central pawns come off and lines open.

plans.reason: White plays for development and f7 pressure.
